page: Microsoft Azure F1as_v7 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the Fasv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1 physical core, 1 thread, and 4.0 GB of system memory. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to its single-core design, the F1as_v7 achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression at 40.93 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 18.11 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark database operations fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory performance is mixed, with small-block cached read bandwidth in the bottom 25% at 216.18 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths reach average tiers at 41.98 GB/sec and 32.1 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1as_v7 offers a low-entry hardware profile with dedicated CPU resources, avoiding the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances. However, the lack of local storage and the single-threaded bottleneck limit its utility for parallelized workloads. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, small-scale LLM inference prototyping, or low-intensity background utility services.
